question.text: Marshall was a member of this political party that advocated for a strong central government.
question.clue: The Coodies were a faction of this party from Maryland.

swap.leadin: This North American war ended with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.
swap.text: Name this war that saw Winfield Scott take the port of Veracruz and others capture forts on the Baja California peninsula.
swap.answerHtml: The Mexican-American War [or Mexican War or U.S.-Mexican War or the Invasion of Mexico]
swap.clue: One battle in this conflict saw a group known as the "boy heroes" unsuccessfully defend Chapultepec Castle from Winfield Scott's forces.

question.leadin: This event saw South Carolina declare the Tariffs of 1828 and 1832 unconstitutional.
question.text: Name this crisis, a forerunner to the pre-Civil War secession.
question.clue: This event, which was almost ended by the Verplanck Bill, led to the passage of the Force Act.

swap.leadin: This country's first attempt at independence was known as the Fredonian Rebellion.
swap.text: Name this state that gained independence from Mexico in an 1836 revolution.
swap.clue: Mirabeau Lamar led this country, and one man who died for this country now lends his name to the Bowie knife.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the 1832 Reform Act.
question.text: The Reform Act was passed while Earl Grey, a member of this party, was prime minister. This party opposed the Tories.
question.clue: Its power diminished as it entered into a coalition with William Gladstone's Liberal Party.

swap.leadin: This battle's namesake mission in San Antonio was defended by such men as Davy Crockett.
swap.text: Name this battle in which Mexican soldiers slaughtered the defending Texans, led by Colonel Travis.
swap.clue: This battle included George C. Kimble's Gonzales Rangers and saw the death of Commander William Travis.

question.text: The Specie Circular was issued by this U.S. president, who liquidated the Second Bank of the U.S. This man created the "Trail of Tears" by ordering the forced march of the Cherokee and other tribes from their homeland.
question.clue: He killed the Nicholas Biddle-led Second Bank of the U.S. with the Specie Circular and signed the Indian Removal Act.

swap.text: Marshall presided over this notable 1824 case in which the Commerce Clause was expanded to include laws relating to navigation. This case arose because of a dispute involving steamship licensing.
swap.answerHtml: Gibbons v. Ogden [accept reverse order; both names necessary; prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: As business manager for the petitioner in this case, Cornelius Vanderbilt operated with a license obtained from the Federal Coasting Act.

question.text: The Second Bank of the United States was once led by this man, who succeeded Langdon Cheves as its president and issued reliable BUS notes that served as a de-facto national currency.
question.clue: This man reached his highest post after the resignation of Langdon Cheves, and he was opposed in that role by Treasury Secretary Roger Taney.

swap.leadin: This man angered Abraham Lincoln by issuing martial law and emancipating the slaves of Missouri in 1861.
swap.text: Name this man, known as "The Pathfinder" for his success on expeditions out west with Kit Carson. He helped wrest the Bear Flag Republic from Mexican control.
swap.clue: He was arrested and court-martialed by Stephen Kearny after he refused to relinquish governorship of California.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the United States' diplomatic relations with Britain and France during the Napoleonic Era.
question.text: Congress passed this piece of legislation thanks to public pressures over incidents like the Chesapeake-Leopard affair. A political cartoon about this act depicts a turtle biting the butt of a man clinging to a barrel.
question.clue: This law, which sought to maintain English and French neutrality during the Napoleonic wars, was replaced by the Non-Intercourse Act and was depicted by Alexander Anderson as a snapping turtle.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the "Corrupt Bargain,"
swap.text: An innocent bystander in the ordeal was what presidential candidate of the Democratic-Republican party? He later served as secretary of the treasury under Madison and Monroe.
swap.clue: This politician became the last presidential candidate ever nominated by a congressional caucus.

question.leadin: Name some dudes who went to the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia.
question.text: This delegate from Massachusetts also later served as a Senator from New York. He ran on two consecutive Federalist tickets in the first decade of 1800s as Vice President.
question.clue: This person ran as a (+) Federalist in the 1816 presidential election with running mate John E. Howard but lost in a landslide to James Monroe.

swap.leadin: This executive order was passed as a result of the increased availability of land following the Indian Removal Act.
swap.text: Name this executive order which mandated the purchase of land only in hard currencies like gold or silver.
swap.clue: Cries to "rescind" this order were common during the Panic of 1837.

question.leadin: This man interviewed the neighbors of the subject of one his biographies, who told him stories about how he had cut down a cherry tree as a child.
question.text: Name this first biographer of George Washington.

swap.leadin: Lesser-known allies with the United States in these clashes were Sweden and the Kingdom of Sicily.
swap.text: Name this series of early 19th-century conflicts against pirates off a namesake coast. President Thomas Jefferson authorized naval involvement in these wars, the first American military crossing of the Atlantic.
swap.clue: During the first of these wars, Stephen Decatur led a daring raid on the enemy-controlled USS Philadelphia and burned it.

question.leadin: James Crawford co-authored a New York Times bestseller titled "Forget [this place]" which examines "the Rise and Fall of an American Myth" in historical records.
question.text: Name this place where the pioneers James Bowie and Davy Crockett died at an 1836 battle, after which the phrase "Remember [this place]" became a rallying cry.
question.answerHtml: Alamo Mission [accept Battle of the Alamo or Forget the Alamo or “Remember the Alamo”; prompt on San Antonio]
question.clue: This San Antonio fort that was besieged by Santa Anna's forces in early 1836.

swap.leadin: Robert Fossier paired this weapon with "The Oath" in his study of ordinary life in the Middle Ages.
swap.text: Identify this type of weapon that also lends its name to a battle where a steamship called The Warrior prevented many Winnebago Indians from fleeing across a river. In that battle named for this weapon, Brigadier General Henry Atkinson delivered a decisive defeat to Black Hawk.
swap.clue: An infamous New Orleans serial killer who usually used this weapon said he would spare anyone who had jazz playing in their homes. Lizzie Borden probably killed her father and stepfather with this type of weapon.

question.leadin: This man's earliest solo works include the Hammerwood Lodge and the former Virginia State Penitentiary.
question.text: Name this man who was appointed surveyor of public buildings by Thomas Jefferson, in which role he put designs of American plants such as corn and tobacco in the interior of the Capitol.
question.clue: In a lull in his career, he designed a steam powered wool mill in Steubenville, Ohio as an offshoot of a partnership to build steamboats with Robert Fulton.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Supreme Court decision FTPE.
swap.text: The Charles River Bridge decision cited this 1810 case dealing with Georgia's Yazoo grants.
swap.clue: This 1810 case that found that a state had no authority to void contracts.
